issues.body: Sections 1.2, 3, 5, and 6 treat update_in_place_capturing as returning a set-valued actual delta. It does not: the DELETE DATA path applies the requested batch and then records that entire batch, including triples absent from the replica. Consequently, naming a masked triple produces a captured delete that fails vis_a validation, so step 5 denies the request. This contradicts the §5 promise that deleting a masked/absent quad is a permitted silent no-op and makes the verdict differ between the proposed semantics and mechanism.
issues.fix_hint: Revise the mechanism to derive effective deletes by intersecting each requested delete batch with the replica state at that operation, or extend capture with an actual-change mode. Specify and test DELETE DATA for (1) absent, (2) masked-but-present, and (3) visible-present triples; the first two must have identical outcomes and effects under the stated semantics. Do not describe the current capture log as an actual set-valued delta until this distinction is addressed.
issues.title: Captured DELETE DATA is not the actual state-changing delta assumed by W1

issues.body: The §6.1 pipeline first runs the complete update against replica_graph and only afterward lowers Clear/Drop into explicit deletes over the replica. At that point the affected replica graph has already been cleared or dropped, so its visible pre-effect triples are unavailable. This is especially incorrect for ordered multi-operation requests: lowering from either the initial or final replica cannot reproduce the state at each structural operation, and flattening effects can change insert/delete ordering.
issues.fix_hint: Require structural lowering during execution, against the replica state immediately before each Clear/Drop, and preserve the ordered effect stream. Alternatively retain per-operation snapshots or reject structural operations in W1. Add a real multi-operation acceptance test such as INSERT; CLEAR; INSERT and verify replay matches execution on the masked replica while masked store triples survive.
issues.title: Structural effects cannot be lowered after capture from the final replica

verdict.summary: The record identifies the existing WHERE-clause disclosure well, but its proposed W1 mechanism does not implement the per-construct semantics it claims. The existing capture API records requested DELETE DATA terms even when absent, and structural effects cannot be lowered from the already-mutated final replica. Both gaps can turn intended silent no-ops into denials or produce an incorrect replay for multi-operation updates.
